purpose: Teach: 爐/駝/實/濤/鵬/鮖/鵝/蛎

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、製鉄の爐、つまり古代炉の考古研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, your paper examined the archaeological research on ancient iron furnaces, didn't it?
lines.style: Gentle confirmation, not interrogation. Calm, steady pace. Eyes warm with genuine interest. A teacher who already knows the answer but wants to hear how you'll tell it.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、駝、つまり駱駝、つまりラクダの民俗利用の研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes—I researched the traditional uses of camels in folk culture for my paper.
lines.style: Straightforward, slightly careful. Modest tone. Speaking clearly but not elaborating—he's learned teachers appreciate precision over flourish. Slight pause after 'Yes' to signal his turn is ready to end.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、旧字「實」、つまり実の文献研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, your paper looked at the literary and textual research on the classical character 實, didn't it?
lines.style: Thoughtful, slower pace. A slight tilt of her head—she's piecing something together as she speaks. Not quizzing him, but genuinely curious about the direction of his work.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、怒濤、つまり大濤の海洋研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes—I examined the oceanographic research on large waves, or tides, in my paper.
lines.style: Patient clarity. Each phrase lands with slight emphasis, like he's learned to structure his answers cleanly. No apology in his tone, but no expansion either. He trusts the information to speak for itself.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、伝説の鳥、鵬の文学的研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, your paper explored the literary research on the mythical bird Peng, didn't it?
lines.style: Gentle curiosity drawing him forward. Slower, more deliberate than before—she's noticing something. Soft undertone of a smile. The kind of teacher who delights when a student's passions emerge.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、伝統魚名の鮖、つまりカジカの分類研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes—I researched the classification of a traditional fish species, kajika, for my paper.
lines.style: Quiet but grounded. His answer is precise, but there's a small note of something beneath—maybe relief that this one came out cleanly. Still measured, still careful, but less hesitant than before.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、家禽の鵝、つまりガチョウの民俗研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, your paper examined the folk research on domesticated geese, didn't it?
lines.style: Warm recognition now. She's speaking slightly slower, with more intention. Not testing him anymore—welcoming him into something. Her tone suggests she's seeing the pattern he might not have noticed in himself.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、旧字「蛎」、つまり牡蠣の表記史を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes—I examined the notational history of the classical character 蛎, the character for oyster, in my paper.
lines.style: Final answer with quiet completion. Slight settling in his posture—he's done. Calm, factual, but with a small breath of relief at the end, like a door closing gently on something he's been holding.
